rationale.conceptual: Established DFT methods (plane-wave PAW-GGA, Birch EOS) applied to a multi-composition alloy/hydride series. Requires understanding of crystallographic Wyckoff positions, convergence criteria, and stabilization energy formulas. It involves careful implementation of several interacting components, but no fundamentally novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: generate four crystal structures, run full geometry relaxations (scored), compute isolated H₂ energy, perform multiple single-point calculations per system for an equation of state, fit Birch EOS, and derive stabilization energies. Orchestration of DFT jobs for different systems and volume points adds complexity beyond a single script.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing DFT results from a small-scale solid-state study. The method (plane-wave PAW-GGA, Birch EOS fitting) is standard but non-trivial; the pipeline involves generating multiple crystal structures, running geometry optimizations, a reference H₂ calculation, and an EOS fit across four compositions. Conceptual difficulty is moderate, execution requires multi-stage orchestration of DFT calculations with post-processing, but no novel algorithms or massive scale.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small unit cells (≤20 atoms), moderate plane-wave cutoff (269.56 eV) → modest RAM (~GB) and CPU-time; no GPU needed.
